Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

retire verb

stop working

also retirement, retired, go into retirement, retiree

classical

Sen. Brev. 3.5: ā quīnquāgēsimō annō in ōtium sēcēdam
M-O s.v. retire

in ōtium sēcēdere

verb phrase

retire (from work or public life)

ōtium is the time free of business (negōtium), and retirement itself (Traupman 371). The law called up no soldier after fifty and summoned no senator after sixty (Sen. Brev. 20.5).

Other words

  • in ōtium venīre — retire, come into one’s leisure

    verb phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.7: cum in ōtium vēnerimus; Traupman 106, 371

  • rude dōnārī — be pensioned off; literally, be given the wooden sword

    verb phrase · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.1.2: dōnātum jam rude; Ov. Tr. 4.8.24: mē quoque dōnārī jam rude tempus erat; M-O s.v. retire; retired

    A gladiator who had earned his release was given a wooden sword (rudis); Horace and Ovid say it of themselves, Cicero of Antony (Phil. 2.74). Retired, rude dōnātus (M-O).

  • in ōtium sē referre

    also used · modern · Traupman 180

    Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections; the classical phrases are those above.

Examples

  • Audiēs plērōsque dīcentēs: 'Ā quīnquāgēsimō annō in ōtium sēcēdam, sexāgēsimus mē annus ab officiīs dīmittet.'

    You will hear most people say: ‘At fifty I shall retire; my sixtieth year will release me from my duties.’Sen. Brev. 3.5

  • Omnem spem dēlectātiōnis nostrae, quam, cum in ōtium vēnerimus, habēre volumus, in tuā hūmānitāte positam habēmus.

    All my hope of the pleasure I mean to have when I retire rests on your kindness.Cic. Att. 1.7

  • mīles ubi ēmeritīs nōn est satis ūtilis annīs, pōnit ad antīquōs, quae tulit, arma Larēs. sīc igitur, tardā vīrēs minuente senectā, mē quoque dōnārī jam rude tempus erat

    When a soldier has served out his years and is no longer much use, he lays the arms he carried before his old household gods; so too, now that slow old age is sapping my strength, it was time for me to be given the wooden swordOv. Tr. 4.8.21–24

See also pension, job, career.
